overview.headline: Volcano hazards that threaten people and property

keyPoints.point: Eruption columns can grow rapidly to more than 12 miles and form eruption clouds.
keyPoints.quote: Eruption columns can grow rapidly and reach more than 12 miles above a volcano in less than 30 minutes, forming an eruption cloud.

keyPoints.point: More than 90% of gas emitted by volcanoes is water vapor with other gases causing acid rain.
keyPoints.quote: More than 90% of all gas emitted by volcanoes is water vapor (steam)

keyPoints.point: Pyroclastic flows can be as hot as 1,500°F and move at speeds of 100 to 150 miles per hour.
keyPoints.quote: These pyroclastic flows can be as hot as 1,500°F and move at speeds of 100 to 150 miles per hour.

keyPoints.point: Lahars are flows composed mostly of volcanic materials that can travel more than 50 miles.
keyPoints.quote: These flows of mud, rock, and water can rush down valleys and stream channels at speeds of 20 to 40 miles per hour and can travel more than 50 miles.

keyTerms.gloss: Solid and molten rock fragments blasted into the air during eruption.
keyTerms.quote: An explosive eruption blasts solid and molten rock fragments (tephra) and volcanic gases into the air with tremendous force.

keyTerms.gloss: Small openings where gases reach the surface when volcano is quiet.
keyTerms.quote: Even when a volcano is not erupting, cracks in the ground allow gases to reach the surface through small openings called fumaroles.

keyTerms.gloss: Irregular mounds of thick lava that squeeze out of a vent.
keyTerms.quote: Dacite and rhyolite lavas often squeeze out of a vent to form irregular mounds called lava domes.

keyTerms.gloss: Flows composed mostly of volcanic materials mixed with mud and water.
keyTerms.quote: Mudflows or debris flows composed mostly of volcanic materials on the flanks of a volcano are called lahars.

keyTerms.gloss: Hot avalanches of ash and rock fragments that move at high speeds.
keyTerms.quote: These pyroclastic flows can be as hot as 1,500°F and move at speeds of 100 to 150 miles per hour.
